口咽癌对侧低位颈部选择性放疗保留后的客观吞咽结局：单中心临床经验

Objective Swallowing Outcomes After Sparing Contralateral Low-Neck Elective Radiotherapy in Oropharyngeal Carcinoma: Single-Institution Clinical Experience.

中文摘要

吞咽困难是口咽鳞状细胞癌（OPSCC）化放疗（CRT）的主要毒性。选择性上颈部照射（UNI），即省略低位颈部，可能降低食管入口肌（EIM）剂量并改善吞咽结局，相较于选择性全颈部照射（WNI）。我们比较了UNI与WNI后的吞咽结局。 2015年至2023年的回顾性综述。 三级学术中心。 我们回顾性审查了接受根治性CRT的OPSCC患者，这些患者进行了基线和治疗后的视频荧光吞咽研究（VFSS）。结局包括吞咽运动学、功能性VFSS指标、喂养管放置和复发。 纳入52例p16阳性OPSCC患者：28例（54%）UNI和24例（46%）WNI。治疗组间T和N分期平衡。UNI和WNI之间的声门上、声门和缩咽肌剂量相似。UNI的EIM剂量低于WNI（29.8 vs 36.1 Gy，P = .011）。与WNI相比，UNI与CRT期间/之后喂养管放置发生率较低相关（22% vs 57%，P = .00643），并且在调整T/N分期和EIM剂量后，CRT后1年喂养管放置风险降低（风险比[HR] 0.25，P = .006）。食管扩张、肺炎或复发的发生率未见差异。在省略的对侧低位颈部未观察到疾病复发。 与WNI相比，UNI与EIM剂量降低和喂养管放置率较低相关，且未影响疾病控制。在需要选择性对侧颈部照射的OPSCC患者中，省略对侧低位颈部是一种有前景的降阶梯策略。

英文摘要

Dysphagia is a major toxicity of chemoradiation (CRT) for oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). Elective upper-neck irradiation (UNI), omitting the low neck, may reduce esophageal inlet muscle (EIM) dose and improve swallowing outcomes compared to elective whole-neck irradiation (WNI). We compared swallowing outcomes after UNI versus WNI. Retrospective review from 2015 to 2023. Tertiary academic center. We retrospectively reviewed OPSCC patients treated with definitive CRT who underwent baseline and post-treatment videofluoroscopic swallow studies (VFSSs). Outcomes included swallowing kinematics, functional VFSS measures, feeding tube placement, and recurrence. Fifty-two patients with p16-positive OPSCC were included: 28 (54%) UNI and 24 (46%) WNI. T and N stages were balanced between treatment groups. Supraglottic, glottic, and constrictor doses were similar between UNI and WNI. EIM dose was lower in UNI than WNI (29.8 vs 36.1 Gy, P = .011). UNI was associated with a lower incidence of feeding tube placement during/after CRT than WNI (22% vs 57%, P = .00643) and reduced hazards of feeding tube placement at 1 year post-CRT when adjusted for T/N stage and EIM dose (hazard ratio [HR] 0.25, P = .006). No differences were seen in the incidence of esophageal dilation, pneumonia, or recurrence. No disease relapse was observed in the omitted contralateral low neck. UNI was associated with reduced EIM dose and lower rates of feeding tube placement compared to WNI, without compromising disease control. In OPSCC patients requiring elective contralateral neck irradiation, omitting the contralateral low neck is a promising de-escalation strategy.
